newsitem.title: UK: Shell profit flat in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Shell profit flat in first quarter.

text.p: Anglo-Dutch oil giant Royal Dutch/Shell Group reported flat first-quarter earnings Thursday, hurt by the strength of the U.S. dollar.
Excluding special items, income rose one percent to 1.545 billion pounds ($2.5 billion) from 1.535 billion ($2.49 billion) a year earlier, the company said.
Shell said profits were held back by the pound's strength, adding that earnings would have risen by seven percent if measured in dollars.

Shell warned that crude oil prices, which have been falling in recent months, could continue to weaken this year. The company said production increases in both OPEC and non-OPEC countries are likely to exceed demand growth, while global inventories are projected to rise.
The company, which is 60 percent owned by Royal Dutch Petroleum and 40 percent by Shell Transport and Trading Co Plc, added it also expected refining margins to remain under pressure.
First quarter earnings in the refining sector were similar to a year ago as lower profits in the United States were offset by an improved performance elsewhere in the world.
Exploration and production earnings rose to their second highest quarterly level ever, but the impact of higher oil prices compared with a year ago was partly offset by lower gas volumes.
In chemicals, earnings rose as cost reductions outweighed lower margins.
